title: Finite-field pro-étale ordinary direct-image finiteness
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, $k$ a field of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and $A$ a finite field of characteristic $\ell$. Let $f:T\to V$ be a finite-type $k$-morphism between finite-type $k$-schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use ordinary uncompleted derived categories of module sheaves over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ on small pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\mathcal B_A(T)$ for the complexes whose cohomology vanishes outside a finite interval and is constructible [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]: there is a finite constructible locally closed stratification on which each cohomology sheaf is pro-étale locally constant with finite-dimensional $A$-module values. Then the ordinary total right derived functor $Rf_*$ [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] of the module direct image $f_*$ [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image], computed by applying $f_*$ to a K-injective resolution, satisfies $Rf_*\mathcal B_A(T)\subseteq\mathcal B_A(V)$. No finiteness, perfection or separable closedness of $k$ is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.2, finite-field specialization, with Lemma 5.4.3 and Theorem 6.7.1; expanded using the existing arbitrary-field étale finiteness node.

proof.text: First check the geometric hypotheses for comparison. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$), and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is quasi-compact. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], both $T$ and $V$ are Noetherian, hence quasi-compact. By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], both are quasi-separated. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (1), applied to $f:T\to V$, makes $f$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. These implications require no separatedness of $f$ or of the structure morphisms.

source.place: Tag 01OY (lemma-locally-Noetherian-quasi-separated); finite-type permanence and qcqs morphism permanence as in the cited nodes

proof.text: We identify the constructibility convention before using comparison. Since $A$ is a finite field, it is Noetherian and its finitely generated modules are precisely its finite-dimensional vector spaces, which are finite sets. On either site, a finite global constructible locally closed stratification is in particular such a stratification locally. Conversely, on a qcqs scheme choose a finite affine open cover carrying the local stratifications. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-stratification-local-gluing-core] to obtain a finite global stratification whose stratum maps factor through the local stratum maps. Pull back each local constant model along this factorization: its trivializing covering pulls back to a covering, on which the same finite $A$-module is constant. Thus the local and global constructibility conditions agree. The argument uses actual stratum morphisms, not only inclusions of their images. In particular the intrinsic pro-étale category $\mathcal B_A(W)$, for $W=T,V$, is the bounded constructible category appearing in [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison].

source.place: Tags 09AJ (definition-constructible), 09AK (lemma-compare-constructible), 09AL (lemma-compare-constructible-derived); global stratification gluing as in the cited node

proof.text:
Take $K\in\mathcal B_A(T)$. Apply the bounded constructible equivalence of [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] with the discrete Noetherian coefficient ring $\Lambda=A$. It gives $G\in D^b_c(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and an isomorphism $\alpha:
u_T^*G\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ in the ordinary pro-étale derived category. Here $
u_T^*$ is the actual intrinsic module inverse image, not a change to condensed or completed coefficients: [lem-pe-coefficient-comparison-derived-functor] identifies its derived functor with termwise inverse image and says that it commutes with every cohomology functor. The module inverse image $
u_W^*$ of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], used by the comparison theorem and in step 7, and the intrinsic module pullback along the constant-section ring map of [lem-pe-coefficient-comparison-data] are both left adjoint to the same module direct image $
u_{W,*}$ (sections on étale objects, with the $A$-action through the constant-section map), so they are canonically isomorphic by uniqueness of adjoints; we use this identification for $W=T,V$ throughout. All comparison hypotheses hold by step 1; $G$ is in particular bounded below.

source.place: Tags 09AK and 09AL; the actual module derived inverse image as in the cited coefficient-comparison node

proof.text: The coefficient ring $A$ is finite and is annihilated by $\ell$. The image of $\ell$ in the field $k$ is nonzero since $p\ne\ell$, hence is invertible. Apply [thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility] to the given morphism between finite-type $k$-schemes, with this ring $A$ and the complex $G$. It gives $H:=Rf_{\mathrm{et},*}G\in D^b_c(V_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ in the ordinary derived category. The cited statement explicitly allows $f$ not separated and places no finiteness, perfection, or separable closedness assumption on $k$.

source.place: statement (ordinary étale finite-type direct-image finiteness, without separatedness); finite-field input in Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 6.7.1

proof.text: We also verify that the derived direct image in the assertion exists on the full ordinary category. Use the small-site universe convention already included in the item. For each of the étale and pro-étale constant-ring sites, [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] makes the category of $A_W$-module sheaves Grothendieck abelian. By [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective] every complex has a K-injective resolution. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] to degreewise $f_*$ followed by derived localization constructs $Rf_*$ and computes it as $f_*I$ on a K-injective representative $I$. Degreewise application of the additive functor $f_*$ respects homotopies, shifts and mapping cones, which is exactly the exact-functor hypothesis on the homotopy categories in the cited theorem.

source.place: Tag 07A5 (section-unbounded), opening paragraphs; Injectives Tag 079P; Derived Categories Tag 070K (lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies)

proof.text: On a bounded-below input, this full-category functor agrees with the usual bounded-below right derived direct image. Indeed, the Grothendieck categories in step 5 have enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. By [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative], any bounded-below input on either site has a bounded-below complex $I$ of injectives representing it, and this $I$ is K-injective. The usual bounded-below derived value is represented by $f_*I$; the full-category value is represented by the same $f_*I$ by [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Therefore comparison on $D^+$ computes the ordinary uncompleted $Rf_*$ of the item on $K$, and the ordinary étale $Rf_*$ on $G$.

Apply [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] to the qcqs morphism $f$ and the bounded-below étale complex $G$. Together with $Rf_{\mathrm{proet},*}(\alpha)$ and step 6, it gives an isomorphism in the full ordinary derived category
$$
u_V^*H=
u_V^*Rf_{\mathrm{et},*}G\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{\mathrm{proet},*}
u_T^*G\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{\mathrm{proet},*}K.$$
By [lem-pe-coefficient-comparison-derived-functor], $\mathcal H^q(
u_V^*H)\cong
u_V^*\mathcal H^q(H)$. By the forward direction of [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison], these are constructible and vanish outside the finite cohomological interval for $H$ from step 4. Step 2 identifies this constructibility with the global finite-stratification condition defining $\mathcal B_A(V)$. Hence $Rf_*K\in\mathcal B_A(V)$, as required.

split_report.blueprint: Realizes the finite-field geometric finiteness input extracted from the internal-Hom finiteness sentence of lem-sfb-dc-hom-preserves, via lem-sfb-finite-field-internal-hom-finiteness. It expands the ordinary Rf_* input using the finite-field specialization of Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 6.7.2 and the current blueprint thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility. The former same_as pointer to lem-sfb-dc-lower-star-preserves was removed because that node has a separated standing setting and condensed-module coefficients; it is not the same statement.

The actual module inverse image and its cohomology compatibility keep the coefficient category and finite cohomological interval explicit.
Existing arbitrary-field ordinary étale finiteness is precisely the geometric input to the finite-field proof of Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 6.7.2.

Generic total-derived-functor computation identifies the K-injective construction, without a completed replacement.
Generic enough-injectives theorem is used only to compare the full and bounded-below derived constructions.
Generic bounded-below K-injective representatives identify the two direct-image constructions on the inputs used here.
The qcqs comparison is the direct-image comparison step of the finite-coefficient Bhatt–Scholze argument.
